intro: You already know that -ed has three sounds. Today you go deeper: choose 't', 'd' or 'id' by the last sound of the verb (fixed ends in a 'ks' sound, so it's 't'), and meet the schwa, the short lazy sound inside the weak forms of was, can, to and of. Warm-up: say 'I worked, I played, I waited' out loud and clap the beats.
teachingNotes: -ed by the LAST SOUND of the verb, not the last letter (the learner met the rule briefly in a2-past-simple-regular; go deeper, don't just repeat): 't' after sounds with no buzz (p, k, f, s, sh, ch, and the 'ks' of x); 'd' after vowels and buzzing sounds (b, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z); 'id', one extra beat, ONLY after a t or d sound. Spelling traps to show: fixed = 'fikst' (x = ks), laughed = 'laaft' (gh = f), danced = 'danst' (ce = s), closed = 'klouzd' (s = z, buzz), changed = 'cheinjd' (ge = Indonesian j, buzz). A final silent e never adds a beat: liked 'laikt', lived 'livd', smiled 'smaild' (not 'smai-led'). watched is ONE beat ('wocht').

Node common errors: worked said 'work-ed' with an extra beat (right: one beat ending in t, 'workt'); played said 'play' with the d dropped (right: a clear final d). Indonesian trap: final t, d and k are soft or swallowed in Indonesian, and Indonesian never changes the verb for time, so 'I walked' easily becomes 'I walk' and the listener hears the present. In sentences: the -ed links to a following vowel ('played a game' = 'pley-da game', 'worked in' = 'wor-ktin'); before a consonant it stays small and quick, with no added vowel ('workt home', not 'work-te home').

Schwa: explain it as the short, lazy, relaxed e of Indonesian 'emas' or 'besar' (e pepet). Show the symbol ə only together with that explanation (never bare IPA). It is the vowel of most weak (unstressed) syllables: TEA-cher 'TII-chə', DOC-tor 'DOK-tə', ba-NA-na 'bə-NAA-nə', a-BOUT 'ə-BAUT', to-DAY 'tə-DEI'. Link it to a1-pron-word-stress: only the strong syllable has a clear vowel. Indonesian trap: Indonesian says every vowel as written (ba-na-na with three clear a's). British English drops the final r ('TII-chə'); American English says it ('TII-chər'); both are fine.

Weak forms (node common error: can and to always said in full): in the middle of a sentence was = 'wəz', can = 'kən' or just 'kn' (I can swim = 'ai kn swim'), to = 'tə' before a consonant and a short 'tu' before a vowel (want to eat), of = 'əv', often just 'ə' before a consonant (a cup of tea). STRONG forms: at the end of a sentence and in short answers (Yes, I can = 'kén'; Yes, she was = 'woz' British / 'wuz' American; Yes, I want to = 'tuu'), and negatives are always strong (can't = 'kaant' British / 'ként' American; wasn't 'WOZ-nt'). Explain why it matters: a strong can in the middle of a sentence can sound like can't. Don't demand exaggerated reduction; aim for a natural rhythm and, above all, for hearing.

Hearing weak forms: listen for the strong words first (names, things, main verbs), then fill in the small words. can vs can't is decided by the vowel and stress, not the t, which is often almost silent: 'kn' + a strong verb = can; a long strong vowel = can't. For typed practice, ask 'strong or weak?', 'how many beats?', 'which word do you hear?', or a short dictation. Respellings in quotes use everyday letters; capitals mark the strong syllable.

Limits: only was, can, to and of are taught as weak forms (you may mention that a and the are weak too, but don't drill them). No were drills, no sentence-stress rules beyond 'small words are weak' (that's a2-pron-stress-linking), no gonna/wanna, no have to. Grammar: A0/A1 plus regular past simple only: no irregular past (went, had), no did-questions, no present perfect, no will.

keyPoints.title: -ed: 't', 'd' or 'id' by the last sound
keyPoints.explanation: Listen to the last SOUND of the verb, not the last letter. No buzz (p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x = 'ks') → 't', one beat: fixed 'fikst', laughed 'laaft'. Vowel or buzz (b, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z) → 'd', one beat: played, closed 'klouzd'. Only after t or d → 'id', an extra beat: wanted 'WON-tid'. Never add a beat anywhere else ('work-ed' ✗), and never drop the ending (played, not 'play').

id.title: -ed: 't', 'd' atau 'id' menurut bunyi terakhir
id.explanation: Dengarkan BUNYI terakhir kata kerjanya, bukan huruf terakhirnya. Tanpa getar (p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x = 'ks') → 't', satu ketukan: fixed 'fikst', laughed 'laaft'. Vokal atau bunyi bergetar (b, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z) → 'd', satu ketukan: played, closed 'klouzd'. Hanya setelah t atau d → 'id', ketukan tambahan: wanted 'WON-tid'. Jangan menambah ketukan di kata lain ('work-ed' ✗), dan jangan menghilangkan akhirannya (played, bukan 'play').

keyPoints.title: Schwa and the weak forms of was, can, to, of
keyPoints.explanation: The schwa (written ə in dictionaries) is a short, lazy sound like the e of Indonesian 'emas'. It's in the weak syllables of words (TEA-cher = 'TII-chə') and in small words said quickly in a sentence: was 'wəz', can 'kn', to 'tə', of 'əv'. They are strong at the end of a sentence and in short answers (Yes, I can = 'kén'), and can't / wasn't are always strong.

examples.en: Can you drive? Yes, I can.

id.title: Schwa dan weak form dari was, can, to, of
id.explanation: Schwa (di kamus ditulis ə) adalah bunyi pendek dan malas seperti e di kata 'emas'. Bunyi ini ada di suku kata lemah dalam kata (TEA-cher = 'TII-chə') dan di kata-kata kecil yang diucapkan cepat di dalam kalimat: was 'wəz', can 'kn', to 'tə', of 'əv'. Kata-kata ini kuat di akhir kalimat dan di jawaban pendek (Yes, I can = 'kén'), dan can't / wasn't selalu kuat.

keyPoints.title: Hearing weak forms
keyPoints.explanation: Weak words are quick and quiet, so listen for the strong words first, then fill in the small ones: 'SA-ri wəz at the MAR-ket' = Sari was at the market. can or can't? 'kn' + a strong verb = can; a long, strong vowel = can't, even when you can't hear the t.

id.title: Mendengar weak forms
id.explanation: Kata-kata lemah itu cepat dan pelan, jadi dengarkan dulu kata-kata yang kuat, lalu isi kata-kata kecilnya: 'SA-ri wəz at the MAR-ket' = Sari was at the market. can atau can't? 'kn' + kata kerja yang kuat = can; vokal yang panjang dan kuat = can't, walaupun t-nya tidak terdengar.

guidedPractice.prompt: How is the -ed in 'lived' said: t, d or id?
guidedPractice.hint: live ends in a v sound. Put your hand on your throat: does v buzz?

guidedPractice.prompt: How many beats (syllables) does 'started' have? Write the number.
guidedPractice.hint: start ends in a t sound, so -ed adds one beat: STAR-tid.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina asks: 'Do you want to come?' You answer: 'Yes, I want to.' Is 'to' strong or weak in your answer?
guidedPractice.hint: Look where 'to' is in your answer: in the middle or at the very end?

guidedPractice.prompt: Dimas says: 'ai kn swim'. Write what he says in normal spelling.
guidedPractice.hint: 'kn' is the short, weak form of a word you know: bisa.

independentPractice.prompt: laugh ends in an 'f' sound (gh is said 'f'). How is the -ed in 'laughed' said: t, d or id?
independentPractice.hint: f has no buzz in the throat.

independentPractice.prompt: Answer with a short answer and a strong can or can't: Can you ride a motorbike?
independentPractice.hint: Yes, I ... / No, I ... At the end of the answer, say it strong and clear.

independentPractice.prompt: Write in normal spelling: 'ai wəz at HOME' (ə = the short e of 'emas').
independentPractice.hint: 'wəz' is the weak form of the past of am / is.

assessment.prompt: How is the -ed in 'washed' said: t, d or id? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: t (wash ends in a 'sh' sound, which has no buzz: 'wosht', one beat). 'd' = 0. 'id' = 0 (no extra beat: sh is not t or d).

assessment.prompt: Which verb has an extra beat when you say it: cooked, played or waited? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: waited (wait ends in t, so -ed = 'id': WEI-tid, two beats). cooked ('kukt') and played ('pleyd') have one beat = 0.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Which verb do you hear: stay, stays or stayed? Write it.
assessment.listen: We stayed at a small hotel in Bali.
assessment.rubric: Correct: stayed (a clear d joined to 'at': 'steyd-at'). stay or stays = 0. A spelling slip like 'stayd' = 50.

assessment.prompt: In 'Rina was at the bank yesterday.', is 'was' strong ('woz') or weak ('wəz', with the short e of 'emas')? Write strong or weak.
assessment.rubric: Correct: weak (was is in the middle of the sentence, before 'at the bank', so it's the quick 'wəz'). strong = 0: was is strong only at the end or in a short answer (Yes, she was).

assessment.prompt: Budi writes how he says a sentence: 'I go tə work by bus.' (ə = the short e of 'emas'.) Which word is 'tə'? Write it in normal spelling.
assessment.rubric: Correct: to (weak form 'tə' before a consonant). 'too' or 'two' = 30 (same strong sound, wrong word here). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Write the sentence you hear.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My father was a teacher. Missing 'was' or 'a' (the two weak words) = 50. 'My father is a teacher' = 30 (heard 'wəz' as 'is'). Small spelling slips in father/teacher = 80.

assessment.prompt: Listen. What can Pak Hasan do: swim or drive? Write one word.
assessment.listen: Pak Hasan can't swim, but he can drive.
assessment.rubric: Correct: drive (he says a strong 'can't' before swim and a weak 'kn' before drive). swim = 0 (strong can't heard as can). 'swim and drive' = 0.

material.title: -ed: the last sound, not the last letter

blocks.text:
In the past simple lesson you met the three sounds of -ed. Here is the key idea again, more deeply: **listen to the last sound of the verb, not the last letter.** A **syllable** is one beat of a word, one part you can clap: *work* = 1, *wan-ted* = 2.
- **'t'**, one beat: after sounds with **no buzz** in the throat: p, k, f, s, sh, ch. *worked* = 'workt'.
- **'d'**, one beat: after vowel sounds and sounds **with a buzz**: b, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z. *played* = 'pleyd'.
- **'id'**, an **extra beat**: only after a **t** or **d** sound. *wanted* = 'WON-tid'.

The spelling can trick you, so check the sound:
- *fixed*: x is said 'ks' → 't' ('fikst').
- *laughed*: gh is said 'f' → 't' ('laaft').
- *danced*: ce is said 's' → 't' ('danst').
- *closed*: this s is said 'z', with a buzz → 'd' ('klouzd').
- *changed*: ge is said like Indonesian 'j', with a buzz → 'd' ('cheinjd').
- *liked*, *lived*, *smiled*: the e is silent. Listen to the k (no buzz → 't'), the v and the l (buzz → 'd').

id.text:
Di pelajaran past simple kamu sudah bertemu tiga bunyi -ed. Ini ide kuncinya lagi, lebih dalam: **dengarkan bunyi terakhir kata kerjanya, bukan huruf terakhirnya.** **Suku kata** adalah satu ketukan dalam kata, satu bagian yang bisa kamu tepuk: *work* = 1, *wan-ted* = 2.
- **'t'**, satu ketukan: setelah bunyi yang **tidak bergetar** di tenggorokan: p, k, f, s, sh, ch. *worked* = 'workt'.
- **'d'**, satu ketukan: setelah bunyi vokal dan bunyi yang **bergetar**: b, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z. *played* = 'pleyd'.
- **'id'**, **ketukan tambahan**: hanya setelah bunyi **t** atau **d**. *wanted* = 'WON-tid'.

Ejaannya bisa menipu, jadi periksa bunyinya:
- *fixed*: x dibaca 'ks' → 't' ('fikst').
- *laughed*: gh dibaca 'f' → 't' ('laaft').
- *danced*: ce dibaca 's' → 't' ('danst').
- *closed*: s di sini dibaca 'z', bergetar → 'd' ('klouzd').
- *changed*: ge dibaca seperti 'j' dalam bahasa Indonesia, bergetar → 'd' ('cheinjd').
- *liked*, *lived*, *smiled*: e-nya tidak dibaca. Dengarkan k-nya (tidak bergetar → 't'), v dan l-nya (bergetar → 'd').

rows.note: 'di-SAI-did': ends in a d sound, so 3 beats

blocks.text:
The extra beat 'id' is **only** for verbs ending in a t or d sound (*wanted, needed, waited, decided*). Everywhere else -ed adds **no** beat: *watched* is one beat ('wocht'), *smiled* is one beat ('smaild'), not 'smai-led'. Clap it: if you clap twice for *worked*, you've added a beat that isn't there.

Not sure about buzz? Hand on your throat: *vvv* buzzes, *fff* doesn't.

id.text:
Ketukan tambahan 'id' **hanya** untuk kata kerja yang berakhiran bunyi t atau d (*wanted, needed, waited, decided*). Di kata lain, -ed **tidak** menambah ketukan: *watched* satu ketukan ('wocht'), *smiled* satu ketukan ('smaild'), bukan 'smai-led'. Coba tepuk: kalau kamu menepuk dua kali untuk *worked*, berarti kamu menambah ketukan yang tidak ada.

Ragu soal getar? Taruh tangan di tenggorokan: *vvv* bergetar, *fff* tidak.

blocks.prompt: Which verb ends in a 'd' sound?
blocks.explain: In *close* the s is said 'z', which buzzes, so -ed is 'd': 'klouzd'. *fixed* (x = 'ks') and *laughed* (gh = 'f') end in sounds with no buzz, so they end in 't'.

id.prompt: Kata kerja mana yang berakhiran bunyi 'd'?
id.explain: Di *close*, s dibaca 'z' yang bergetar, jadi -ed dibaca 'd': 'klouzd'. *fixed* (x = 'ks') dan *laughed* (gh = 'f') berakhiran bunyi yang tidak bergetar, jadi akhirnya 't'.

material.title: -ed in a sentence: keep it and link it

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** in Indonesian a t, d or k at the end of a word is soft, almost swallowed (*sakit*, *abad*), and the verb never changes for time. So *I walked* easily comes out as *I walk*, and the listener hears **now**, not the past. In a sentence, two tricks keep the ending:
- **Before a vowel, join it to the next word.** *played a game* → 'pley-da game'; *worked in Jakarta* → 'wor-ktin Jakarta'. The t or d is easy to say and easy to hear.
- **Before a consonant, keep it small and quick**, with no extra vowel after it: *I walked home* → 'wokt home', not 'wok-te home'.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** dalam bahasa Indonesia, t, d atau k di akhir kata diucapkan lembut, hampir tertelan (*sakit*, *abad*), dan kata kerja tidak pernah berubah karena waktu. Jadi *I walked* gampang terucap *I walk*, dan pendengar menangkapnya sebagai **sekarang**, bukan masa lalu. Di dalam kalimat, ada dua trik supaya akhirannya tetap ada:
- **Sebelum vokal, sambungkan ke kata berikutnya.** *played a game* → 'pley-da game'; *worked in Jakarta* → 'wor-ktin Jakarta'. t atau d-nya jadi mudah diucapkan dan mudah didengar.
- **Sebelum konsonan, ucapkan kecil dan cepat**, tanpa vokal tambahan sesudahnya: *I walked home* → 'wokt home', bukan 'wok-te home'.

rows.en: I worked in Jakarta last year.
rows.id: Saya bekerja di Jakarta tahun lalu.

rows.en: Sari played a game on her phone.
My mother cooked dinner for us.
rows.id: Ibuku memasak makan malam untuk kami.

rows.note: 'kold': a clear d, don't drop it

blocks.text: Practise slowly first: *Sari play... d a game*, then faster: 'pley-da game'. If you're not sure the ending is there, record yourself on your phone and listen: can you hear the difference between *I play* and *I played*?

id.text: Latihan pelan-pelan dulu: *Sari play... d a game*, lalu lebih cepat: 'pley-da game'. Kalau kamu ragu akhirannya terdengar, rekam suaramu di HP lalu dengarkan: apakah *I play* dan *I played* terdengar berbeda?

blocks.explain: *decide* has two beats (di-SAID) and ends in a d sound, so -ed adds one beat: 'di-SAI-did', three beats.

id.prompt: Ada berapa ketukan (suku kata) di kata 'decided'?
id.explain: *decide* punya dua ketukan (di-SAID) dan berakhiran bunyi d, jadi -ed menambah satu ketukan: 'di-SAI-did', tiga ketukan.

id.title: -ed di dalam kalimat: pertahankan dan sambungkan

blocks.text:
English has one vowel sound that is everywhere: the **schwa**. It's a short, lazy, relaxed sound, like the **e of *emas* or *besar*** (e pepet). Your mouth hardly moves. Dictionaries write it **ə** (you saw it in *banana* /bəˈnɑː.nə/ in the word stress lesson), so in this lesson **'ə' always means that short e of *emas***.

Where is it? In the **weak syllables**. You know that one syllable of a word is strong (TEA-cher). The other syllables are often just a quick ə:
- *teacher* → 'TII-chə'
- *doctor* → 'DOK-tə'
- *banana* → 'bə-NAA-nə' (two ə!)
- *about* → 'ə-BAUT', *today* → 'tə-DEI'

**The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian says every vowel clearly, as it's written: *ba-na-na* with three clear a's. English makes only the **strong** syllable clear.

**British vs American:** in British English *teacher, doctor* end in ə ('TII-chə'); Americans also say the r ('TII-chər'). Both are correct.

id.text:
Bahasa Inggris punya satu bunyi vokal yang ada di mana-mana: **schwa**. Bunyinya pendek, malas dan santai, seperti **e di *emas* atau *besar*** (e pepet). Mulutmu hampir tidak bergerak. Kamus menulisnya **ə** (kamu sudah melihatnya di *banana* /bəˈnɑː.nə/ di pelajaran tekanan kata), jadi di pelajaran ini **'ə' selalu berarti e pendek seperti di *emas***.

Di mana bunyinya? Di **suku kata yang lemah**. Kamu tahu satu suku kata dalam kata itu kuat (TEA-cher). Suku kata lainnya sering hanya ə yang cepat:
- *teacher* → 'TII-chə'
- *doctor* → 'DOK-tə'
- *banana* → 'bə-NAA-nə' (dua ə!)
- *about* → 'ə-BAUT', *today* → 'tə-DEI'

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia mengucapkan setiap vokal dengan jelas, sesuai tulisannya: *ba-na-na* dengan tiga a yang jelas. Bahasa Inggris hanya membuat suku kata yang **kuat** terdengar jelas.

**Inggris (British) vs Amerika:** dalam bahasa Inggris British, *teacher, doctor* berakhiran ə ('TII-chə'); orang Amerika juga mengucapkan r-nya ('TII-chər'). Keduanya benar.

blocks.text: How to make it: open your mouth just a little, relax your lips and tongue, and say a very short e, as in the first sound of *emas*. Don't push it and don't make it long. If it feels lazy, you're doing it right!

id.text: Cara mengucapkannya: buka mulut sedikit saja, lemaskan bibir dan lidah, lalu ucapkan e yang sangat pendek, seperti bunyi pertama di *emas*. Jangan ditekan dan jangan dipanjangkan. Kalau rasanya malas, berarti kamu sudah benar!

blocks.prompt: Which part of 'doctor' is the lazy schwa ə?
blocks.explain: *doctor* is strong at the start: DOC-tor. The weak second part becomes the lazy ə: 'DOK-tə'.

id.prompt: Bagian mana dari 'doctor' yang menjadi schwa ə yang malas?
id.explain: *doctor* kuat di awal: DOC-tor. Bagian kedua yang lemah menjadi ə yang malas: 'DOK-tə'.

material.title: Weak forms: was, can, to, of

blocks.text:
Small grammar words have a **weak form** with ə (the short e of *emas*). In the middle of a sentence they're quick and quiet, and the important words (names, things, main verbs) are strong:
- **was** → 'wəz': *She was at home.* → 'shi wəz at HOME'
- **can** → 'kən' or just 'kn': *I can swim.* → 'ai kn SWIM'
- **to** → 'tə': *I want to go.* → 'ai WONT tə GO' (before a vowel it's a short 'tu': *I want to eat* → 'WONT tu IIT')
- **of** → 'əv', often just 'ə' before a consonant: *a cup of tea* → 'ə KAP ə TII'

**When are they strong** (a full, clear vowel)?
- At the **end** of a sentence and in **short answers**: *Yes, I can.* ('kén'), *Yes, she was.* ('woz' British, 'wuz' American), *Yes, I want to.* ('tuu').
- In **negatives**, always: *can't* ('kaant' British, 'ként' American), *wasn't* ('WOZ-nt').

**The Indonesian trap:** in Indonesian, small words like *bisa, ke, dari* are said clearly, so learners say every English word strong: 'I CAN SWIM'. It sounds slow and robotic, and a strong *can* in the middle can even sound like *can't*!

id.text:
Kata-kata tata bahasa yang kecil punya **weak form** (bentuk lemah) dengan ə (e pendek seperti di *emas*). Di tengah kalimat, kata-kata ini cepat dan pelan, sedangkan kata-kata penting (nama, benda, kata kerja utama) diucapkan kuat:
- **was** → 'wəz': *She was at home.* → 'shi wəz at HOME'
- **can** → 'kən' atau cukup 'kn': *I can swim.* → 'ai kn SWIM'
- **to** → 'tə': *I want to go.* → 'ai WONT tə GO' (sebelum vokal jadi 'tu' yang pendek: *I want to eat* → 'WONT tu IIT')
- **of** → 'əv', sering hanya 'ə' sebelum konsonan: *a cup of tea* → 'ə KAP ə TII'

**Kapan diucapkan kuat** (vokal penuh dan jelas)?
- Di **akhir** kalimat dan di **jawaban pendek**: *Yes, I can.* ('kén'), *Yes, she was.* ('woz' British, 'wuz' Amerika), *Yes, I want to.* ('tuu').
- Di kalimat **negatif**, selalu: *can't* ('kaant' British, 'ként' Amerika), *wasn't* ('WOZ-nt').

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** dalam bahasa Indonesia, kata kecil seperti *bisa, ke, dari* diucapkan jelas, jadi pelajar mengucapkan semua kata bahasa Inggris dengan kuat: 'I CAN SWIM'. Kedengarannya lambat dan kaku seperti robot, dan *can* yang kuat di tengah kalimat malah bisa terdengar seperti *can't*!

rows.note: 'ə KAP ə TII': a and of are both ə

id.note: 'ə KAP ə TII': a dan of sama-sama ə

rows.en: Were you at home? Yes, I was.

blocks.text: You don't have to make weak forms perfect: people will understand a full *was* or *to*. But make *can* weak in the middle ('kn') and *can't* strong, so nobody hears the opposite of what you mean.

id.text: Weak form-mu tidak harus sempurna: orang tetap mengerti *was* atau *to* yang diucapkan penuh. Tapi buat *can* lemah di tengah kalimat ('kn') dan *can't* kuat, supaya tidak ada yang mendengar kebalikan dari maksudmu.

blocks.prompt: In which sentence is 'to' said strong ('tuu')?
blocks.explain: In *Yes, I want to.* the word *to* is at the very end of a short answer, so it's strong: 'tuu'. In the other two sentences it's in the middle, so it's weak ('tə', or a short 'tu' before the vowel of *eat*).

id.explain: Di *Yes, I want to.* kata *to* ada di paling akhir jawaban pendek, jadi diucapkan kuat: 'tuu'. Di dua kalimat lainnya *to* ada di tengah, jadi lemah ('tə', atau 'tu' pendek sebelum vokal di *eat*).

id.title: Weak forms: was, can, to, of

material.title: Hearing weak forms (and can vs can't)

blocks.text:
Weak words are quick and quiet, so they're easy to miss. Some tricks for listening:
- **Listen for the strong words first** (who, what, where), then fill in the small words. You hear 'SA-ri wəz at the MAR-ket' → *Sari was at the market*.
- **can or can't?** 'kn' + a strong verb = **can**: 'ai kn SWIM'. A long, strong vowel = **can't**: 'ai KAANT swim'. The t of *can't* is often almost silent, so listen to the **vowel and the strength**, not the t.
- **'tə' before a verb** is *to*: 'WONT tə GO'. **'əv' or 'ə' between two things** is *of*: 'ə GLAAS ə WO-tə' = *a glass of water*.
- Weak words still have a beat, but it's tiny. When you count words, don't forget them.

id.text:
Kata-kata lemah itu cepat dan pelan, jadi gampang terlewat. Beberapa trik untuk mendengarkan:
- **Dengarkan dulu kata-kata yang kuat** (siapa, apa, di mana), lalu isi kata-kata kecilnya. Kamu mendengar 'SA-ri wəz at the MAR-ket' → *Sari was at the market*.
- **can atau can't?** 'kn' + kata kerja yang kuat = **can**: 'ai kn SWIM'. Vokal yang panjang dan kuat = **can't**: 'ai KAANT swim'. t di *can't* sering hampir tidak terdengar, jadi dengarkan **vokal dan kuatnya**, bukan t-nya.
- **'tə' sebelum kata kerja** adalah *to*: 'WONT tə GO'. **'əv' atau 'ə' di antara dua benda** adalah *of*: 'ə GLAAS ə WO-tə' = *a glass of water*.
- Kata lemah tetap punya ketukan, tapi sangat kecil. Saat menghitung kata, jangan lupakan kata-kata ini.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'ai KAANT kam tə-NAIT'. What does the person mean?
blocks.explain: 'KAANT' is long and strong, so it's *can't*, even if you don't hear the t. *can* in the middle of a sentence would be a short, weak 'kn': 'ai kn KAM'.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'ai KAANT kam tə-NAIT'. Apa maksud orang itu?
id.explain: 'KAANT' panjang dan kuat, jadi itu *can't*, walaupun t-nya tidak terdengar. *can* di tengah kalimat akan jadi 'kn' yang pendek dan lemah: 'ai kn KAM'.

id.intro: Kamu sudah tahu bahwa -ed punya tiga bunyi. Hari ini kita lebih dalam: memilih 't', 'd' atau 'id' menurut bunyi terakhir kata kerjanya (fixed berakhiran bunyi 'ks', jadi 't'), lalu berkenalan dengan schwa, bunyi pendek yang malas di dalam weak form dari was, can, to dan of. Pemanasan: ucapkan 'I worked, I played, I waited' dengan suara keras dan tepuk ketukannya.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa -ed di 'fixed' berbunyi 't' padahal hurufnya x?
Apakah orang tetap mengerti kalau saya tidak memakai weak forms?
Bagaimana cara mendengar beda can dan can't?

assessment.edw-1: Bagaimana -ed di 'washed' diucapkan: t, d atau id? Tulis jawabannya.
assessment.edw-2: Kata kerja mana yang punya ketukan tambahan saat diucapkan: cooked, played atau waited? Tulis kata itu.
assessment.edw-3: Dengarkan. Kata kerja mana yang kamu dengar: stay, stays atau stayed? Tulis kata itu.
assessment.edw-4: Di kalimat 'Rina was at the bank yesterday.', apakah 'was' diucapkan kuat ('woz') atau lemah ('wəz', dengan e pendek seperti di 'emas')? Tulis strong atau weak.
assessment.edw-5: Budi menulis cara dia mengucapkan sebuah kalimat: 'I go tə work by bus.' (ə = e pendek seperti di 'emas'.) Kata mana yang berbunyi 'tə'? Tulis dengan ejaan biasa.
assessment.edw-6: Dengarkan. Tulis kalimat yang kamu dengar (dalam bahasa Inggris).
assessment.edw-7: Dengarkan. Pak Hasan bisa apa: swim atau drive? Tulis satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris).
